description: Example response from ThreatLens Analyzer API showing expected structure

threats.title: API Gateway Spoofing Attack
threats.description: Attackers may impersonate the API Gateway to intercept or manipulate client requests. Without proper certificate validation and mutual TLS, clients cannot verify the authenticity of the gateway.

threats.title: Authentication Token Forgery
threats.description: Weak token generation or validation mechanisms could allow attackers to forge authentication tokens and impersonate legitimate users.

threats.title: Database Tampering via SQL Injection
threats.description: Insufficient input validation in services could lead to SQL injection attacks, allowing unauthorized modification of database records.

threats.title: Data Integrity Violation
threats.description: Lack of integrity checks on data flows could allow attackers to modify data in transit between services.

threats.title: Insufficient Authentication Logging
threats.description: Without comprehensive audit logs, failed authentication attempts and suspicious activities cannot be traced or investigated.

threats.title: Request Repudiation Risk
threats.description: Lack of non-repudiation mechanisms allows users to deny actions performed through the API gateway.

threats.title: Database Credential Exposure
threats.description: Database credentials stored in configuration files or environment variables without encryption pose a significant information disclosure risk.

threats.title: Sensitive Data Leakage in Cache
threats.description: Caching sensitive information without encryption could expose confidential data if the cache is compromised.

threats.title: Message Queue Data Exposure
threats.description: Unencrypted messages in the queue could be intercepted, revealing sensitive business data or user information.

threats.title: API Rate Limiting Bypass
threats.description: Insufficient rate limiting allows attackers to overwhelm the API gateway with requests, causing denial of service.

threats.title: Resource Exhaustion Attack
threats.description: Processing expensive queries without resource limits could exhaust service resources and cause service disruption.

threats.title: Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
threats.description: Uncontrolled connection creation could exhaust database connection pools, preventing legitimate requests.

threats.title: Privilege Escalation via Token Manipulation
threats.description: Weak authorization checks could allow users to escalate privileges by manipulating authentication tokens.

threats.title: Unauthorized Data Access
threats.description: Insufficient authorization controls could allow users to access data beyond their permission level.

threats.title: API Gateway Authorization Bypass
threats.description: Flaws in the gateway's authorization logic could allow attackers to bypass access controls and reach protected endpoints.

mitigations.title: Implement Comprehensive API Security Controls
steps: Deploy mutual TLS (mTLS) for client authentication
Implement rate limiting with adaptive throttling (e.g., 100 requests/minute per IP)
Add request signing to prevent tampering
Enable WAF (Web Application Firewall) with OWASP rules
Implement comprehensive logging and monitoring

mitigations.title: Strengthen Authentication Mechanisms
steps: Use strong JWT tokens with RS256 signing algorithm
Implement token rotation and expiration (15-minute access tokens)
Add multi-factor authentication (MFA) for sensitive operations
Deploy comprehensive audit logging for all authentication events
Implement account lockout after 5 failed attempts

mitigations.title: Secure Database Access and Operations
steps: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements exclusively
Encrypt data at rest using AES-256 encryption
Implement database-level access controls and least privilege
Enable database audit logging for all modifications
Use encrypted connections (TLS) for all database communications

mitigations.title: Implement Data Protection Controls
steps: Add input validation and sanitization for all requests
Implement fine-grained authorization checks (ABAC or RBAC)
Add data integrity verification using checksums or signatures
Implement connection pooling with max limits (e.g., 20 connections)
Add circuit breakers for dependent service failures

mitigations.title: Secure Cache Implementation
steps: Encrypt sensitive data before caching
Use Redis authentication (requirepass)
Enable Redis TLS for encrypted connections
Implement cache key namespacing to prevent collisions
Set appropriate TTL values to minimize exposure

mitigations.title: Secure Message Queue Operations
steps: Encrypt messages using envelope encryption
Implement message signing for integrity verification
Use authenticated AMQP connections with TLS
Add message validation and schema enforcement
Implement dead letter queues for failed messages

assumptions: All services are deployed in a trusted private network
HTTPS/TLS is properly configured with valid certificates
Database credentials are managed using a secrets management system
Regular security patches and updates are applied to all components
uncertainties: The specific authentication mechanism (OAuth, JWT, etc.) is not clearly specified
Data encryption methods for sensitive information are not detailed in the diagram
Network segmentation and firewall rules between trust zones are unclear
